items.article: Vaping could cost users £600 more a year from today, as the Government introduces new taxes in a bid to create a 'smoke-free generation'. Published: 02:00, 1 October 2026 | Updated: 09:29, 1 October 2026 Vaping could cost users £600 more a year from today, under a new tax crackdown aimed at creating a 'smoke-free generation'. A new levy of £2.20 per 10ml of vape liquid means a heavy user getting through around 270 bottles a year could face the £600 annual hit, while a bottle currently marketed at around £3.99 could now cost almost £7. Smokers will also be hit, with a 44p rise on a typical pack of 20 cigarettes – equivalent to around £160 a year for someone smoking a pack a day. Combined with other duty increases, the overall rise is expected to be about £1.20 a pack, which could see heavy smokers spending an extra £440 a year. A typical 50g pouch of tobacco is also expected to rise by around £4.20, amounting to almost £110 extra a year for someone getting through a pouch every fortnight – or £218 for those buying one a week.

Customers can pre-book the facelift for a Rs 21,000 token amount through Honda's website or authorised dealerships. The teaser gives away several design elements of the Honda Elevate facelift. The SUV will continue with its familiar overall silhouette, but the front-end treatment gets a noticeable refresh. One of the key changes is the new connected-style LED DRL setup, which gives the Elevate a more contemporary appearance. The grille also looks like a redesigned unit, while the Honda logo is now positioned higher on the bonnet, adding a slightly different visual identity to the front.
